measurementCondition: 60-second aggregate and per-process /proc/stat and /proc/<pid>/stat time-delta sample; all 4 cores online; light real-world background activity (OneWifi, snmpd, and napi/phy0 Wi-Fi softirq threads all show measurable, nonzero activity) but no controlled client/traffic load applied. Not a controlled multi-client or steering-load test.
notes: First real per-process CPU breakdown captured for this profile (prior captures had only the aggregate figure). Per-process percentages are normalized to % of total system capacity across all 4 cores, matching the aggregate figure's own normalization — NOT % of a single core, consistent with the same correction applied to the EthWAN WiFi Router companion file. othersCpuPercent (1.92%) covers kernel worker/softirq threads plus many near-idle kernel/IRQ threads individually below measurable resolution at this sample rate. OneWifi is the largest single consumer at 0.66% (of total system capacity); onewifi_em_agent — despite its extreme and growing memory footprint (see memory-footprint companion file, ~364 MiB) — shows minimal CPU activity here (0.01%), consistent with idle/light-load conditions rather than active mesh operation; this is notable given the process's memory size and worth re-checking once the memory growth is better understood. This remains an idle/light-load result; a loaded sample (active client traffic, steering) has not yet been collected.
